notes: IMPORTANT MECHANICAL NOTE for re-readers: digicoll record 102021 has NO land-case PDF; it serves 171 page JPEGs at https://digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu/record/102021/files/cubanc_1_2_000NNNNNa_k.jpg. Transcript stamped page N = image number 23958+N (image 00023959 is absent; 00023957 = red portfolio cover). Substance: Vallejo's 1852 petition (p5) claims an 1834 grant whose papers were lost, then 'he applied in 1843 for new papers'; the expediente translation begins p45 and its own recital reads 'in the year one thousand eight hundred and thirty-[four/five] there was granted to him by the Government, and he now possesses, the place of Petaluma, which was confirmed by the Most Excellent Territorial Deputation; but the original titles having been mislaid...' (the numeral word is genuinely ambiguous at this resolution between 'four' and 'five'; Hoffman's table for this case says 1843 anyway). Manuel Jimeno's report p46: 'it having been previously given to him.' So an earlier (Figueroa-era) concession is ACKNOWLEDGED in the file but no Figueroa document survives in it; the operative, confirmed, and patented title is Micheltorena's of Oct 22 1843 (10 leagues) plus a June 22 1844 sale of a 5-league extension (petition p5). Hoffman 1862 (1843 / Micheltorena) agrees with the case file against the register on BOTH flagged fields. Register era tag 'figueroa' should follow the correction to micheltorena, or the register should carry both dates explicitly.

notes: MECHANICS: this PDF is 467MB / 680 pages and cannot be opened whole; I extracted page ranges with pypdf. Stamped '410 ND PAGE n' foliation runs about 3-5 pages behind the PDF page index (PDF 4 = stamped 1; PDF 60 = stamped 56; PDF 100 = stamped 95; PDF 118 = stamped 112) because blank versos and oversize sheets are interleaved. SUBSTANCE: Inigo's claim was split - Walkinshaw (case 125) claimed the half Inigo sold him, Thomas Campbell intervened for 400 acres (supplementary petition PDF p12 / stamped p8, tracing M.M. Wambough June 1847 -> Asa W. Finley June 9 1847 -> Campbell Oct 26 1853), and Inigo himself filed a supplemental petition for the remaining portion; the parties stipulated (PDF p16 / stamped p12) that 'both of said claims being for portions of the same original grant'. CAUTION for the register: witness Jose Antonio Alviso, PDF p23 (stamped p19), swore Inigo 'had a grant prior to that year [1844], from Governor Alvarado', and Hoffman's own table credits 'Juan B. Alvarado and Manuel Micheltorena' - so there are apparently TWO concessions, an earlier Alvarado one (c. 1840, alleged in the petition PDF p10) and Micheltorena's of 15 Feb 1844. The Spanish decree I could read at stamped p71 carries no legible date or signature on that leaf, so I graded year/governor from the two sworn pleadings rather than from the title itself; a re-reader wanting the title verbatim should read stamped pages 55-71 (PDF ~59-75), which hold the Surveyor General's certified 17-page tracing of the archive expediente (certificate of John C. Hays, 4 March 1854, PDF p75).

notes: The register's own patent_to field ('Joaquin Gutierrez and Maria Estefana, daughter of Fructuoso del Real') already carries the correct grantee surname, so the grantee field can be fixed from within the register's own data. Chain: Alvarado's provisional concession 28 Oct 1837 to Fructuoso del Real (1 league, El Potrero, Carmel valley), extended 'for the years 1839 and 1840'; juridical possession was blocked by a boundary conflict with Esteban Munras's Rancho San Francisquito (stamped pp. 22-23, 28); Fructuoso died c. 1845 leaving widow Yginia and daughters Maria Josefa, Maria Teodora and Maria Estefana; Josefa and Teodora deeded their interests to Gutierrez 25 Aug 1853, leaving Estefana a one-third (the amended petition of 28 May 1855, stamped pp. 18-19, asked 5/6 - 1/6 but the Board decreed 2/3 - 1/3). Deposition of W.E.P. Hartnell, stamped p6: 'The Indian Fructuoso first occupied that land as early as 1837'; deposition of Jose Abrego, stamped p7: 'occupied by an Indian, a native of the Mission of San Carlos whose name was Fructuoso del Real'. MECHANICS: stamped '333 SD PAGE n' runs 2-7 pages behind the PDF page index and the gap widens through the file (PDF 3 = stamped 1; PDF 23 = stamped 18; PDF 47 = stamped 40); the transcript's own internal cross-references (opinion 'vide page 44') are one system further off from the stamped foliation.

name.evidence: PDF p2 (stamped p1) transcript title page: 'TRANSCRIPT OF THE PROCEEDINGS IN CASE NO. 2, Maria de la Soledad Ortega de Arguello et als CLAIMANTS vs. THE UNITED STATES, DEFENDANT, FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Las Pulgas"'; Secretary's certificate PDF p434 (stamped p388) 'for the place known by the name of Las Pulgas'. Register 'Pulgas' = the same place (Hoffman 'Las Pulgas').

year.evidence: Opinion of the majority of the Board (Com. Alpheus Felch), PDF p429 (stamped p383): 'Applying these views to the case under consideration we conclude that the title of the land did not pass to the heirs of Arguello by virtue of the Order of Concession of NOV. 26, 1835 nor by the approval of the Territorial Deputation, and that it could pass only by final title papers under the 8th Art. of the Regulation of 1828 which it is not claimed was issued. We also conclude that the conditional document of the 27th Nov. did not, notwithstanding the subsequent approval of the Deputation, have the effect to pass the legal estate...' and PDF p431 (stamped p385): 'we are satisfied that the claimants are justly entitled to a confirmation, COMMENSURATE WITH THE DESCRIPTION IN THE CONDITIONAL GRANT OF NOV 27 and of which juridical possession was given.' The Mexican papers of record are therefore both of November 1835. Claimants' petition, PDF p19-20 (stamped p17-18): '...on the 26th (Twenty Sixth) day of November in said year of 1835 issue[d] a decree of concession of said lands to said Minor heirs of Don Luis Arguello... that subsequently to wit on the 18th day of December of said year said Territorial Deputation granted its approval to the said decree of concession... making the same final and definitively binding.'

governor.evidence: The operative documents are of November 1835, i.e. the MEXICAN period, not Spanish. Claimants' petition PDF p19 (stamped p17) names the granting officer: the October 1835 decree in their favour 'was made on the 3rd day of October 1835 by Don Jose Castro who was on that day the Political Chief or Governor of Alta California', and it was 'the said Governor or Political Chief' who on 26 November 1835 issued the decree of concession. No Spanish-period title paper appears among the exhibits, and the Board's opinion (PDF p429-431 / stamped p383-385) rests entirely on the 1835 documents.

grantee.evidence: The 1835 concession ran to Luis Arguello's HEIRS, not to Luis Arguello himself, who was already dead: Board's opinion PDF p429 (stamped p383) 'the title of the land did not pass to THE HEIRS OF ARGUELLO by virtue of the Order of Concession of Nov. 26, 1835'; petition PDF p18 (stamped p16) 'said Don Luis Arguello died about the year 1830 leaving a widow, your present petitioner the said Dona Soledad, and the following named children and heirs'; decree PDF p432 (stamped p386) confirms to 'Maria de la Soledad Ortega de Arguello One equal undivided half thereof, Jose Ramon Arguello One equal undivided fourth part thereof, Luis Antonio Arguello One equal undivided tenth part thereof, and S. M. Moses three equal undivided twentieth parts.' Register 'Luis Arguello' names the right family and the person to whom the claimants traced their title (and the person to whom the petition says Governor Sola made a title c. 1820-21), so this is a shorthand rather than a substitution of a U.S.-era claimant; Hoffman also writes 'Luis Arguello'.

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 archival cover 'Land Case 54 ND'; every leaf stamped '54 ND'; transcript title page PDF p2 'IN CASE NO. 2'; PDF p4 (stamped p2) 'ordered to be filed and docketed with No. 2'; District Court wrapper PDF p450 (stamped p403) 'U.S. Dist. Court No. 54, Arguello et als vs. The United States'. Register 'ND 054' and Hoffman (commission 2 / court 54) both match; filename cubanc_lcf_nd054.pdf agrees.

outcome.evidence: Commission DECREE, PDF p432-433 (stamped p386-387), filed 12 Oct 1853, signed Alpheus Felch, Thompson Campbell, R. Aug. Thompson: 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the said claim of the Petitioners is valid as to that portion of the land described in the petition which is bounded... on the South by the Arroyo or Creek of San Francisquito, on the North by the Creek San Mateo, on the east by the Esteros or waters of the Bay of San Francisco and on the west by the eastern borders of the Valley known as the "Canada de Raimundo", said land being of the extent of four leagues in length and one in breadth... and it is therefore hereby decreed that the said land be and the same is hereby confirmed to them'; BUT 'as to the portion of the premises described in said petition which is not included within the boundaries above mentioned, the claim of the petitioners is adjudged NOT TO BE VALID and their application for a confirmation thereof is therefore DENIED.' The claim was thus confirmed only in part, the Canada de Raymundo being excluded. The case then went to the U.S. District Court (transcript of the record filed 26 July 1854, PDF p435; order allowing all parties to take further evidence, filed 29 Sept 1854, PDF p450 = stamped p403; further claimants' petition at stamped p433). I did not read the District Court decree, so the final extent is not verified here.

corrections.year: 1835 - the Order of Concession of 26 November 1835, approved by the Territorial Deputation 18 December 1835, together with the conditional title of 27 November 1835 on which the Board actually confirmed (opinion PDF p429-431 / stamped p383-385). Hoffman 1862 ('1835') agrees with the case file against the register. The register's 1820 rests on the claimants' unsupported recital (petition PDF p18 / stamped p16) that 'about the year 1820 or 1821 Don Pablo Vicente de Sola, being then Governor of Alta California... made a new title to the said Rancho or tract of land to Don Luis Arguello'; no such document is in evidence and the Board never mentions it.
corrections.governor: Not a Spanish governor. The granting authority of record is the Mexican political chief / acting governor of Alta California in 1835, named in the claimants' petition (PDF p19 / stamped p17) as Jose Castro, with the Territorial Deputation's approval of 18 Dec 1835.
corrections.grantee: Strictly, the minor heirs of Don Luis Arguello (widow Maria de la Soledad Ortega de Arguello and children), the 1835 concession having issued after Luis Arguello's death c. 1830.

notes: MECHANICS: 647MB / 594 PDF pages, extracted in ranges with pypdf. TWO page systems: a pencil number top-left = the TRANSCRIPT's own pagination (1-437, certified by Secretary George Fisher, PDF p434), and a stamped '54 ND PAGE n' = the Bancroft portfolio foliation, which runs behind it because blank versos are unstamped and the District Court papers are foliated in the same stamped run. The transcript's internal cross-references ('opinion vide page 410', 'decree vide page 436') are to the PENCIL system: the opinion ends at pencil 435 = stamped 385 = PDF 431, the decree is pencil 436-437 = stamped 386-387 = PDF 432-433. In the stamped system PDF = stamped + 47 in the 380-433 range. SUBSTANCE: this is the heavily contested Las Pulgas case (Board split; Com. R. A. Thompson filed a partial dissent concurring in the result, transcript p394; Coppinger/Greer contestants for the Canada de Raymundo in case No. 21; Gervasio Arguello moved to contest in case No. 367 and was denied on an equally divided Board, stamped p8). The claimants' own chain of title as pleaded is: (1) a license from Governor Diego de Borica to Don Jose Dario Arguello as far back as 1795, preserved only 'in traditions and the memory of the old inhabitants'; (2) a new title from Governor Pablo Vicente de Sola to Don Luis Arguello 'about the year 1820 or 1821'; (3) the 1835 Castro decrees. Only (3) is documentary, and only (3) was adjudicated. The register's year/governor/era therefore record an undocumented Spanish-period tradition rather than the grant of record. The Board held the claim rested in EQUITY, not in legal title, because no final title papers under Art. 8 of the Regulation of 1828 were ever issued.

Leese, "Punta de Pinos", Transcript of the Record from Board of U.S. Land Commissioners in Case No. 353, Filed Dec. 19th 1854.' Register 'SD 169' and Hoffman (commission 353 / court 169) both match; filename cubanc_lcf_sd169.pdf agrees.

outcome.evidence: DECREE OF CONFIRMATION, PDF p50 (stamped p44), filed 13 June 1854, signed Alpheus Felch and R. Aug. Thompson, Commissioners: 'In this case on hearing the proofs and allegations it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the Petitioners is valid and it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed to the said Claimants with[in] following shares and proportions to wit: To the said Jacob P. Leese one undivided moiety, to the said Milton Little one undivided fourth part and to the said Santiago Gleason one undivided fourth part of the premises so confirmed to them.' Opinion PDF p49 (stamped p43): 'The conditions of the grant appear from the evidence to have been fully complied with... A Decree of Confirmation will accordingly be entered in favor of the Claimants for their respective interests in the premises.' The case then went to the U.S. District Court (transcript filed 19 Dec 1854, PDF p53). Register 'Confirmed' matches; the later patent (1880, GLO 279, to Henry de Graw et al) is outside this file.

corrections.year: 1833 for the original grant (Figueroa to Armenta, 24 May 1833 per the Board's opinion and decree; the expediente's own concession decree is dated Monterey 13 May 1833 and the formal title evidently issued 24 May). If the register wants to keep both title acts, the field should read '1833; 1844' to match its own two-governor / two-grantee fields. Hoffman 1862 ('1833') agrees with the case file against the register. The register's era tag 'micheltorena' should likewise become 'figueroa' (or carry both).

notes: This record is the mirror image of the dominant error class: the register got the GRANTEES right (Armenta and Abrego, not the claimant Leese) but dated the rancho by the later of the two grants. Full documented chain from the Board's opinion (PDF p48-49 / stamped p42-43): (1) original grant, Figueroa to Jose Maria Armenta, 24 May 1833, approved by the Territorial Deputation (the register's own petition text, PDF p6 / stamped p4, dates that approval 17 May 1834); (2) judicial act of sale 16 June 1844 by Armenta's widow and his heirs Jose, Jose Antonio and Christoval Armenta to Jose Abrego; (3) new grant, Micheltorena to Abrego, 4 Oct 1844, 'in confirmation of said act of sale'; (4) Abrego and wife to Milton Little, Jacob P. Leese, James (Santiago) Gleason and Thomas O. Larkin, 15 Jan 1850; (5) Larkin to Leese, 8 July 1852 for $3,000 (deed at PDF p46 / stamped p40). Leese's attorney had filed the claim in Leese's name alone for the whole tract; Leese's own affidavit of 21 April 1854 (PDF p45 / stamped p39) explains the error and the co-tenants were admitted by amended petition, which is why the decree splits the confirmation 1/2 - 1/4 - 1/4. MECHANICS: stamped '169 SD PAGE n' = PDF page - 2 at the front of the file and PDF page - 6 by stamped p39; transcript is 49 pages, certified by Secretary George Fisher 14 Dec 1854 (PDF p52).

name.evidence: PDF p1 red cover 'CASE NO. 130 NORTHERN DISTRICT / LA PURISIMA CONCEPCION GRANT / JUANA BRIONES CLAIMANT'; grant translation PDF p27 (stamped p22) 'the place named La Purisima Concepcion'; Commission decree PDF p33 (stamped p28) 'is known by the name of La Purisima Concepcion'.

year.evidence: Sworn translation of the grant, PDF p27 (stamped p22): 'Given at Monterey the Capital of the Department of Californias on the thirtieth day of the month of June, one thousand eight hundred & forty. (Signed) Juan B. Alvarado. (Sgd) Manl Jimeno, Secretary of State'; note appended PDF p28 (stamped p23) 'His Excellency the Governor thus ordered, decreed & signed. Monterey June 30th 1840.' Board's opinion PDF p32 (stamped p27): 'bearing date the 30th of June 1840.'

governor.evidence: Grant translation PDF p27 (stamped p22) headed 'Juan B. Alvarado, Constitutional Governor of the Department of the Californias' and signed by him; earlier marginal decrees of 12 June 1837, 10 Dec 1839 and 22 May 1840 in the same expediente are all '(Signed) Alvarado' (PDF p26 / stamped p21). Board's opinion PDF p32 (stamped p27): 'a grant made by Governor Juan B. Alvarado'.

grantee.evidence: Grant translation, PDF p27 (stamped p22): 'Whereas Gorgonio, a neophyte of the ex-mission of Santa Clara, has, in his own name & in that of his son Jose Ramon, petitioned for the place named La Purisima Concepcion... I HAVE BY THESE PRESENTS GRANTED TO SAID GORGONIO & TO HIS SON JOSE RAMON, the ownership of the aforementioned place of La Purisima Concepcion, in extent one sitio de ganado mayor (one square league).' Board's opinion PDF p32 (stamped p27): 'founded on a grant made by Governor Juan B. Alvarado, to an emancipated Neophyte of the Mission of Santa Clara, named Gorgonio & his son Jose Ramon... The present claimant derives her title by virtue of a conveyance made to her with the sanction of the Government BY THE SAID GRANTEES Gorgonio & Jose Ramon on the 7th of November 1844.' Juana Briones is the purchaser/claimant, not the grantee: her own 1852 petition PDF p9 (stamped p4) says Alvarado 'granted to Jose Gregorio & his son Jose Ramon, emancipated Neophytes of the Mission of Santa Clara... the tract of land known by the name of La Purisima Concepcion', and that they 'sold & conveyed in due form to the petitioner' on 7 Nov 1844.

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red cover 'CASE NO. 130 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p2 archival note 'LAND CASE 130 ND, 171 pages'; transcript title PDF p5 (stamped p1) 'IN CASE NO. 119'; PDF p7 (stamped p2) 'ordered to be filed and docketed with No. 119'; Secretary's certificate PDF p34 (stamped p29) 'in Case No. 119 on the Docket of the said Board, wherein Juana Briones is the Claimant... for the place known by the name of "La Purisima Concepcion"'. Register 'ND 130' and Hoffman (commission 119 / court 130) both match; filename cubanc_lcf_nd130.pdf agrees.

outcome.evidence: Board's opinion by Com. R. Aug. Thompson, PDF p32 (stamped p27): 'The case presents no point of doubt or difficulty... THE CLAIM IS THEREFORE CONFIRMED', filed 11 April 1854. DECREE OF CONFIRMATION PDF p33 (stamped p28): 'it is adjudged by the Board that the claim of the petitioner is valid, & it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed. The land of which confirmation is made, is situated in the County of Santa Clara, & is known by the name of La Purisima Concepcion, being the same which has been held & occupied by the present claimant since the year 1844', signed Alpheus Felch, Thompson Campbell, R. Aug. Thompson, Commissioners, filed 11 April 1854. Register 'Confirmed' matches. The portfolio runs to 171 pages, so a District Court record follows the 27-page Commission transcript; I did not read it, and the 1871 patent (GLO 175) is outside the file.

corrections.grantee: Jose Gorgonio and his son Jose Ramon, emancipated neophytes of Mission Santa Clara, per the sworn translation of Alvarado's grant of 30 June 1840 (PDF p27 / stamped p22) and the Board's opinion (PDF p32 / stamped p27). Juana Briones de Miranda bought the rancho from them for $300 by deed of 7 November 1844, executed before the alcalde of San Jose with Micheltorena's licence; she is the U.S.-era claimant, not the grantee. Hoffman 1862 ('Jose Gorgonio and Jose Ramon') agrees with the case file against the register. Dominant error class.

notes: Documented chain: (1) petition of 'Citizen Jose Gorgonio, together with Jose Ramon & Calistro, persons of the same class, all three being neophytes of the Mission of Santa Clara', Pueblo of Alvarado, 25 Nov 1836 (translation PDF p24-26 / stamped p19-21), reciting a piece of land already granted to Gorgonio and Jose Ramon 'by the deceased Senor Figueroa' and complaining that Tulare Indians had wounded the son and burned the house; (2) Alvarado's emancipation order, Santa Clara 12 June 1837; (3) Alvarado's decrees of 10 Dec 1839 and 22 May 1840 ordering measurement; (4) the GRANT, Alvarado to Gorgonio and his son Jose Ramon, Monterey 30 June 1840, one square league, boundaries 'on the west the sierra, on the north west & north the Arroyo del Matadero, on the south and east the Arroyo of San Antonio'; (5) Juana Briones's petition to Micheltorena of 30 Oct 1844 for licence to buy, Micheltorena's decree of the same date and Manuel Jimeno's referral to the magistrate of San Jose (translations PDF p28-29 / stamped p23-24); (6) the sale, San Jose Guadalupe, 7 Nov 1844, signed with crosses by Jose Gorgonio and Jose Ramon before alcalde Maximo Martinez, and Gorgonio's confirmatory instrument of 25 June 1847 acknowledging $300 (PDF p30 / stamped p25). Witness Maximo Martinez, PDF p12 (stamped p7): 'It was first occupied in 1837 by Jose Gorgonio, a Neophyte of the Mission of Santa Clara & his family... The grant was made in 1840 to Jose Gorgonio & his family. The present claimant Briones purchased the rancho of Gorgonio in 1844 by the permission of Gov. Micheltorena.' MECHANICS: stamped '130 ND PAGE n' = PDF page - 5 throughout the front of the file; the Commission transcript is 27 pages, certified by Secretary George Fisher 30 Oct 1854 (PDF p34), and the rest of the 171-page portfolio is the District Court record.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red cover 'CASE NO. 175 NORTHERN DISTRICT / LAS PUTAS GRANT / MARIA ANASTASIA HIGUERA, ET AL CLAIMANT'; transcript title PDF p5 (stamped p1) 'FOR THE PLACE NAMED "Las Putas"'; Board's opinion PDF p69 (stamped p58) 'For the place called Las Putas in Yolo County, containing eight square leagues of land'.

year.evidence: Board's opinion, PDF p69 (stamped p58): 'In support of this Claim the Petitioners have produced in evidence a grant of the land in question made by Governor Manuel Micheltorena to the brothers Jose de Jesus and Sisto Berryesa DATED NOVEMBER 3rd 1843, the approval of the assembly is waived and possession is proved.' Decree of confirmation PDF p72 (stamped p61): 'being the same land which was granted to said Jose de Jesus and Sisto Berryesa in 1843.' Register 1843 agrees; Hoffman agrees.

governor.evidence: Board's opinion PDF p69 (stamped p58): 'a grant... made by GOVERNOR MANUEL MICHELTORENA'. Claimants' petition PDF p11-12 (stamped p5-6) traces Micheltorena's successive decrees of 26, 27, 28, 30 and 31 October 1843 on the brothers' petitions, the last 'ordering the said Secretary to issue the title for which said Petitioners had prayed'.

grantee.evidence: Board's opinion PDF p69 (stamped p58): the grant was 'made by Governor Manuel Micheltorena TO THE BROTHERS JOSE DE JESUS AND SISTO BERRYESA'. PDF p72 (stamped p61) is explicit about the register's confusion: 'Among the documentary evidence introduced into this case are two deeds of the premises claimed, one from Jose de Jesus Berryesa to Anastasia Higuera, HIS WIFE, and the other from Sisto Berryesa to Nicolasa Higuera HIS WIFE. The Petition in the case asks a confirmation in the name of these two grantees, THE WIVES OF THE PERSONS TO WHOM THE ORIGINAL GRANT WAS MADE BY THE GOVERNOR. If the husbands were not themselves joined as petitioners in this case a question not free from difficulty would arise as to the effect of the conveyances from husband to wife.' Claimants' petition PDF p11 (stamped p5) likewise: 'on the 11th day of February 1842 the said Jose Jesus Berryesa and Sisto Berryesa... made their Petition in writing signed by them addressed to the Military Commandant of Sonoma praying for license to occupy provisionally eight sitios de ganado mayor... the said land being known as Las Putas.'

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red cover 'CASE NO. 175 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p2 archival note 'Land Case no. 175, Northern District'; transcript title PDF p5 (stamped p1) 'IN CASE NO. 236'; PDF p7 (stamped p2) 'ordered to be filed and docketed with No. 236'; Secretary's certificate PDF p75 (stamped p63) '67 pages... in Case No. 236 on the Docket of the said Board'; District Court wrapper PDF p76 'U.S. District Court, Northern District of California, No. 175, The United States vs. Maria Anastasia Higuera et al de Berreyesa, Transcript of the Record from the Board of U.S. Land Commissioners in Case No. 236, Filed February 5th 1855.' Register 'ND 175' and Hoffman (commission 236 / court 175) both match; filename cubanc_lcf_nd175.pdf agrees.

outcome.evidence: Board's opinion PDF p72 (stamped p61): 'as they all joined in the Petition and as the title in them is without controversy, we see no difficulty in entering a decree of Confirmation according to the case made in the Record. CONFIRMED', filed 5 Sept 1854. DECREE OF CONFIRMATION PDF p72-73 (stamped p61-62): 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the claim of the Petitioners is valid and it is therefore decreed that the same be confirmed. The lands of which confirmation is hereby made are situated in Yolo County and known by the name of Las Putas... being a deep valley bounded by the Range of hills which encircle it named Loyaca, Cerro Bali and Un cantol [Uncastol], containing eight square leagues a little more or less, the foot of said hills being the boundaries', signed Alpheus Felch, R. Aug. Thompson, S.B. Farwell, filed 5 Sept 1854. The United States APPEALED: Attorney General to U.S. Attorney, Washington 7 April 1855, PDF p77 (stamped p64), 'the appeal in the district court of the United States for the Northern district of California WILL BE PROSECUTED by the United States.' Register 'Confirmed' matches the Commission decree; the District Court outcome is not in the pages read, but the register's patent of 5 Jan 1863 (GLO 83) is consistent with the confirmation standing.

corrections.grantee: Jose de Jesus Berreyesa and Sisto Berreyesa, brothers, per Micheltorena's grant of 3 November 1843 as recited in the Board's opinion (PDF p69 / stamped p58) and its decree (PDF p72 / stamped p61). Maria Anastasia Higuera de Berreyesa and Maria Nicolasa Higuera de Berreyesa are the WIVES of the two grantees and took by deed from their husbands; they are the named U.S.-era claimants (and, per the register, the patentees). Hoffman 1862 ('Jose de Jesus y Sisto Berreyesa') agrees with the case file against the register. A variant of the dominant error class: the register carries the claimant/patentee rather than the Mexican grantee.

notes: Chain as pleaded (petition PDF p11-12 / stamped p5-6): 11 Feb 1842, Jose de Jesus and Sisto Berreyesa petition the military commandant of Sonoma for leave to occupy eight sitios provisionally, and Salvador Vallejo grants the licence by marginal order the same day; 16 July 1843 the brothers petition the Governor for the grant; Micheltorena's decrees follow on 26, 27, 28, 30 and 31 October 1843 (the brothers protesting on 28 Oct that the conditions first imposed 'would render the grant in a great measure unavailable'), and the title issued 3 November 1843. The Board waived the Departmental Assembly's approval. Note for anyone reconciling acreage: the Board wrestled at length with the 'bounded by the range of hills' description, since Aaron Vandom's 1852 survey of the exterior lines along the mountain crests returned 103[4],645 acres against the eight leagues intended, and it confirmed by the grant's own natural boundaries with the eight-league limit controlling (PDF p70-71 / stamped p59-60). The register's patented acreage of 35,515.82 reflects that later resolution. MECHANICS: stamped '175 ND PAGE n' = PDF page - 6 at the front and PDF page - 11 by stamped p58; the transcript is 67 pages, certified by Secretary George Fisher 31 Jan 1855 (PDF p75).
